text:
maria_support: heads up — customer reported intermittent streaming failures from hosted API. says client sees "broken pipe" and then our logs show 502 for the same request. repro attached.

maria_support: stack: curl --http1.1 -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' -d '{\"model\":\"openid/xl\",\"input\":\"hello\"}' 

sahil_eng: looking. Is this specific to one region or model?

maria_support: customer on us-west1, model pinned to openid/xl-v2. They said it started after a deploy yesterday. rate ~30 rps, single connection per request, chunked encoding enabled.

emily_runtime: can you paste the gateway logs? I want connection close semantics.

maria_support: snippet from gateway: 

```
2026-02-15T18:34:12.542Z INF conn_id=abc123 start stream request
2026-02-15T18:34:13.121Z ERR upstream write failed: write tcp 10.2.1.3:443->10.3.5.7:52000: write: broken pipe
2026-02-15T18:34:13.122Z WARN classify as 502 due to upstream write error
```

emily_runtime: hmmm gateway treats any ECONN* as 5xx. But the client actually sent FIN first? That would be a client disconnect not server error. Do we have HTTP connection state logs?

jordan_devx: customer also attached client side trace: they see "RST_STREAM" or plain TCP FIN depending on client lib. Might be mobile. They say sometimes we return a 502 and charge them.

sahil_eng: two root causes I can think of: 1) client aborts mid-stream and our gateway erroneously maps to upstream failure; 2) load spike causes kernel-level EPIPE while upstream still producing. We need to differentiate.

emily_runtime: actionable steps: enable conn-level debug on gateway (we have a flag), capture both upstream and downstream teardown reasons, and correlate request id. Also add metrics: downstream-client-aborts vs upstream-writes-fail. Right now they both map to same error bucket.

maria_support: customer asked for repro steps they can run. i'll share this quick script they used: 

```
# python quick repro
import requests, time
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', json={'model':'openid/xl-v2','input':'x'*2000}, stream=True, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer ' + token})
for line in r.iter_lines():
    print(line)
    time.sleep(0.01)
    if random.random() < 0.02:
        break  # simulate client abort
```

jordan_devx: good. can we reproduce inside our test lab by simulating mobile libs? i can run a fuzzer that does FIN vs RST mid-chunk.

emily_runtime: also check chunked transfer encoding handling in the gateway. there was a recent change that aggressively reuses connections and assumes upstream flush; if a downstream abort comes during a partial chunk, it may surface as upstream write error.

sahil_eng: i found a matching trace from last night's deploy: gateway v2.14.1 changed the write loop. patch note: "treat EPIPE as hard upstream failure" — that's probably the bug.

maria_support: customer understandably upset about being billed for failed responses. Can we add an immediate mitigation? rollback or server-side retry semantics?

emily_runtime: mitigation: revert the change that conflates downstream abort with upstream error, and add a short-term rule: if upstream write fails with EPIPE and downstream connection shows FIN/RST within 200ms prior, classify as client-abort (4xx client_disconnect) and don't count as 5xx for billing.

sahil_eng: i can prepare a hotfix to differentiate errno (EPIPE vs EINVAL) and check downstream socket state before classifying. will open PR and patch the release line.

jordan_devx: i'll prep a support note template and a repro harness so customers can validate the fix. includes suggested client workaround: set keepalive and send a small final chunk to avoid abrupt RST on mobile.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2177, severity=medium, assignee=sahil_eng, start=1842109876

maria_support: customer asked for ETA for rollback. sahil — can you estimate?

sahil_eng: can get a hotfix in the next 4 hours, deploy to canary and run repro harness. if green, promote to region in 8 hours.

emily_runtime: i'll add a dashboard card for downstream-aborts vs upstream-write-errors and a logsearch saved query: 

query: "upstream write failed" OR "downstream FIN" | correlate request_id

maria_support: thanks team. i'll keep customer updated and include the incident id.

(threads end)
